events.text: Silvio Baldini resigned from his post on 31 March 2008.
events.subject: part_of_self
events.quote: Baldini resigned from his post on 31 March 2008

events.text: Baldini was replaced by Walter Zenga.

events.text: Zenga was confirmed in charge of the team for the upcoming 2008–09 season.
events.subject: self
events.quote: Zenga was successively confirmed in charge of the team for the upcoming 2008–09 season

events.text: On 5 June 2009, Zenga left Catania to be the manager at Palermo.

events.text: Zenga was replaced by Gianluca Atzori.
events.subject: self
events.quote: He was replaced by Gianluca Atzori

events.text: On 8 December 2009, Siniša Mihajlović was appointed new head coach of Catania, taking over from Atzori.

events.quote: On 8 December 2009 , Siniša Mihajlović was appointed new head coach of Catania , taking over from Atzori

events.text: After Mihajlović's departure to Fiorentina, Catania appointed Marco Giampaolo as new head coach for the 2010–11 season.
events.subject: self
events.quote: Catania appointed Marco Giampaolo as new head coach for the 2010–11 season

events.text: In January 2011, Catania decided to remove Giampaolo from his position.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In January 2011 , Catania decided to remove Giampaolo from his position

events.text: Catania replaced Giampaolo with Diego Simeone.
events.subject: self
events.quote: replace him with former Argentine star Diego Simeone

events.text: Simeone parted company with Catania by the end of the season after only four months in charge.

events.quote: to part company by the end of the season , after only four months in charge of the team

events.text: Catania appointed 37-year-old Vincenzo Montella as replacement.

events.text: Rolando Maran came in the 2012–13 season and guided Catania to a record-breaking season with 56 points from 38 Serie A matches.
